To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

antibiotic concentrations that do not cause a measurable reduction in microbial biomass and metabolic activity in stream biofilms can still have significant effects on microbial communities and their metabolic activity.

1) the addition of erythromycins, trimethoprin, and clindamycins had no effect on the microbial communities in the effluent dominated praire streams; 2) the addition of antibiotics to the stream had no effect on microbial activity; 3) the addition of the antibiotics had no effect on bacterial diversity.

the addition of the antibiotic erythromycin to the stream had no significant effect on the microbial community structure of the biofilms, whereas trimethoprim caused a significant shift in microbial community structure, with a significant decrease in the relative abundance of Proteobacteria and an increase in Firmicutes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of antibiotic pollution on microbial communities in a prairie stream.
the effect of antibiotic exposure on the structure and function of the microbial community in an effluent-dominated stream.
the effects of antibiotic pollution on microbial communities in an effluent dominated stream.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results from this study indicate that the addition of antibiotics to an effluent dominated stream does not have a negative effect on microbial community structure or function.
the effects of the three antibiotics were different in the stream, and that the antibiotics had the greatest effect on the microbial community in the presence of the other two antibiotics.
the use of antibiotics in aquaculture has a significant impact on the environment and the aquatic life.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of antibiotics in the field can have detrimental effects on microbial communities, but the effects are dependent on the antibiotic used and the community composition of the stream.
the effects of antibiotics on the microbial communities in the environment are complex and depend on the antibiotic concentration and duration of exposure.
we are able to use the microbial community structure of the stream biofilm to predict the community structure in the laboratory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
antibiotics can affect the microbial community in ways that are not easily detected by standard molecular techniques.
antibiotics have the potential to alter stream microbial communities in ways that are relevant to ecosystem functioning.

the antibiotic resistance genes we found are not unique to the prairie pothole region, but are widespread in the environment and in the human microbiome, which suggests that these genes are ancient and likely have been present in humans since before the agricultural revolution.
